exampleAnswers.title: Calculating a Determinant After Switching Two Rows

question.text: Suppose $X$ is a $5\times5$ matrix and $\det(X)=55.$ The matrix $Y$ is obtained from $X$ by applying the elementary row operation $R_5 \leftrightarrow R_3$ (switching the fifth and the third rows). What is the value of $\det(Y)?$
question.explanation:
Since swapping any two rows changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite sign, we have

\begin{align} \det (Y) &= - \det (X) \\[3pt] &= - (55) \\[3pt] &= -55. \end{align}

question.text: Suppose $A$ is a $6\times6$ matrix and $\det(A)=35.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation $R_1:= -\dfrac{3}{5}R_1.$ What is the value of $\det(B)?$
question.explanation:
The row operation applied to $A$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $-\dfrac{3}{5}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

\begin{align} \det(B) &= -\dfrac{3}{5} \det(A) \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{3}{5} \cdot 35 \\[5pt] &= -21. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating a Determinant After Multiplying a Matrix by a Scalar

question.text: Suppose $C$ is a $3\times3$ matrix and $\det(C)=-5.$ What is the value of $\det(-4C)?$
question.explanation:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

\begin{align*} \det(k \cdot C) = k^n \cdot \det(C). \end{align*}

In our case, we have $k=-4$ and $n=3.$ Therefore,

\begin{align} \det(-4C) &= (-4)^3 \cdot \det(C) \\[3pt] &= (-64) \cdot (-5) \\[3pt] &= 320. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating a Determinant After Applying Several Elementary Operations

question.text: Suppose $U$ is a $4\times4$ matrix and $\det(U)=21.$ The matrix $V$ is obtained from $U$ by applying the elementary row operations $R_3: = R_3 + (-7)R_4$ and $R_3 := \dfrac{1}{3}R_3.$ What is the value of $\det(V)?$
question.explanation:
First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

  • The operation $R_3:= R_3 + (-7)R_4$ involves adding a multiple of one row to another row, so it does not change the determinant.

  • The operation $R_3 := \dfrac{1}{3}R_3$ involves multiplying a row by $\dfrac{1}{3},$ so the determinant is multiplied by $\dfrac{1}{3}$ as well.

Therefore, we only have to multiply the determinant by $\dfrac{1}{3}.$ Consequently, we get

\begin{align} \det (V) &= \dfrac{1}{3} \det (U) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot 21 \\[5pt] &= 7. \end{align}

example.title: Calculating a Determinant After Applying Several Elementary Operations

question.text: Suppose $B$ is a $3\times3$ matrix and $\det(B)=-7.$ The matrix $C$ is obtained from $B$ by applying the elementary row operations $R_2 := 2R_2$ and $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_3.$ What is the value of $\det(C)?$
question.explanation:
First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

  • The operation $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_3$ involves swapping two rows, so it changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.

  • The operation $R_2 := 2R_2$ involves multiplying a row by $2,$ so the determinant is multiplied by $2$ as well.

Therefore, we have to change the sign of the determinant to the opposite one and multiply by $2$ as well. Consequently, we get

\begin{align} \det (C) &= 2\cdot (- \det (B)) \\[3pt] &= - 2\det(B) \\[3pt] &= -2\cdot (-7) \\[3pt] &= 14. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying a Row Operation Given the Connection Between Two Determinants

question.text:
Given that $\det(A)=\det(B),$ which of the following elementary row operations transforms matrix $A$ to matrix $B,$ where

\[ A= \begin{bmatrix} 1& 5& 3\\ 2& 4& -2\\ 2& 8& -2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B= \begin{bmatrix} 1& 5& 3\\ 2& 4& -2\\ 0& -2& -8 \end{bmatrix}? \]
question.explanation:
Since $\det(A)=\det(B)$, the row operation applied to $A$ must be to add or subtract a multiple of one row to another row. In other words, it is of the form \[ R_j := R_j + (k)R_i, \quad i \neq j. \]

By considering the given row operations that are of the above form, we notice that

\[ \begin{align*} \det(A) &= \begin{vmatrix} 1& 5& 3\\ 2& 4& -2\\ 2& 8& -2 \end{vmatrix} & R_3 &:= R_3 + (-2)R_1 \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 1& 5& 3\\ 2& 4& -2\\ 0& -2& -8 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \det(B). \end{align*} \]

Therefore, the required row operation is

\[ R_3 := R_3 + (-2)R_1. \]

example.title: Identifying a Row Operation Given the Connection Between Two Determinants

question.text: Consider the matrices given below. Given that $A$ and $B$ are row equivalent matrices and $\det(A) = 6$, find $\det(B).$ \[ A= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2& -1\\ -2 & 2& -2\\ -5& 6 & 3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2& -1\\ -5 & 6& 3\\ -2& 2 & -2 \end{bmatrix}? \]
question.explanation:
Notice that $B$ can be obtained from $A$ by swapping the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows.

This changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one. Therefore, we obtain

\begin{align} \det (B) &= - \det (A) \\[3pt] &= - (6) \\[3pt] &= -6. \end{align}

question.explanation:
Since $\det(A)=\det(B)$, the row operation applied to $A$ must be to add or subtract a multiple of one row to another row. In other words, it is of the form \[ R_j := R_j + (k)R_i, \quad i \neq j. \]

By considering the given row operations that are of the above form, we notice that

\[ \begin{align*} \det(A) &= \begin{vmatrix} 1& 2& 4\\ 2& 4& -1\\ 3& 2& 1 \end{vmatrix} & R_2 &:= R_2 + (-2)R_1 \\[5pt] &= \begin{vmatrix} 1& 2& 4\\ 0& 0& -9\\ 3& 2& 1 \end{vmatrix} \\[5pt] &= \det(B). \end{align*} \]

Therefore, the required row operation is

\[ R_2 := R_2 + (-2)R_1. \]
